sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE P. SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company against the judgment and award dated 02.02.2022 passed by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Kalaburagi, [for short 'Tribunal'] in MVC No.802/2019.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge and
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. One Sidramappa met with an accident on 04.04.2019 and died.
His wife and children filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.19,75,000/-.
The Tribunal considered the entire materials on record and awarded Rs.11,99,436/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Aggrieved by the said order, Insurance Company filed this appeal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6773 HC-KAR 3.
Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.

4. The main contention of the appellant/Insurance Company is that the Tribunal ought to have deducted 50% of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses since claimant Nos.2 and 3 are the major sons of the deceased and they are not dependent on the income of the deceased,
hence, the Tribunal erred in deducting 1/3.

It is also contended that as admitted by PW1/wife of the deceased in her deposition the deceased was aged 68 years at the time of accident, but the Tribunal erroneously held the age of the deceased as 60 years and applied multiplier of '9' instead of '5'.
It is further contended that the Tribunal erred in adding 10% future prospects.
Therefore, he requested to allow the appeal and reduce the compensation amount reasonably.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 3/claimants that the compensation NC: 2025:KHC-K:6773 HC-KAR awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and it needs no interference.
6.
The husband of claimant No.1 met with the accident on 04.04.2019.
In Ex.P7 - Post Mortem Report his age was shown as 60 years.

Even PW1 in her deposition stated the age of the deceased was 60 years and though she admitted the birth year of the deceased as 1951 she has not filed any The Branch Manager Cholamandalam Ms ... vs Kasturibai W.O Siudramma Jamadar And ... on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38269920/

sentences.text: 3 age proof.
Therefore, considering the evidence of PW1 and Post Mortem Report, the Tribunal has considered the age of deceased as 60 years and applied the multiplier of '9'.
This Court finds no reason to interfere with the said order.

7. Further, in the absence of proof of income the Tribunal considered the notional income of the deceased at Rs.13,750/- as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2019, added 10% towards future prospects and rightly deducted 1/3rd of total income towards personal expenses of the deceased and awarded Rs.10,49,436/- towards loss NC: 2025:KHC-K:6773 HC-KAR of dependency to the claimants, which needs no interference by this Court.

The Tribunal observed that claimant No.1 - wife of the deceased is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and claimant Nos.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium, in total Rs.1,20,000/-.

The Tribunal has rightly awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under the conventional heads as per the citation in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi, and it also needs no interference by this Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In view of the above, the appeal is devoid of merits and liable to be dismissed.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is dismissed.
(ii) Appellant - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount NC: 2025:KHC-K:6773 HC-KAR along with interest within four weeks from the date of this judgment.

(iii) On such deposit, claimant Nos.2 and 3/children of the deceased are permitted to withdraw Rs.1,50,000/- each along with interest accrued on it and claimant No.1/wife of the deceased is permitted to withdraw the remaining amount along with interest accrued on it.
(iv) Statutory deposit of 25% is to be transmitted to the Tribunal.
Counsel for respondent No.6 is directed to file Vakalat within two weeks.
